Seedance 2.0 Mini is a ByteDance video generation model in the Seedance 2.0 series. It supports text-to-video, image-to-video with a first frame or first and last frames, and reference-to-video, with audio on by default.

README

Complete guide to using bytedance/seedance-2-mini

Seedance 2.0 Mini API: Text, Image and Reference to Video

Seedance 2.0 Mini is a ByteDance video generation model in the Seedance 2.0 series, offered on Kie.ai as bytedance/seedance-2-mini. It supports three input modes—text-to-video, image-to-video (first or first and last frames), and reference-to-video (images, videos, audio)—and outputs 480p or 720p video of 4 to 15 seconds, or a model-chosen length, with audio on by default.

Seedance 2.0 Mini API Parameters

Send requests to POST /api/v1/jobs/createTask with model set to bytedance/seedance-2-mini. Image-to-video (first frame), image-to-video (first and last frames) and multimodal reference-to-video are mutually exclusive and cannot be combined in the same request.

ParameterDetails
modelRequired. Set to bytedance/seedance-2-mini.
promptRequired. Text prompt from 3 to 20000 characters.
first_frame_urlOptional. Image URL or asset://{assetId} for the opening frame in image-to-video mode. Cannot be combined with any reference_* field.
last_frame_urlOptional. Image URL or asset://{assetId} for the closing frame when used with first_frame_url. Cannot be combined with any reference_* field.
reference_image_urlsOptional. Up to 9 images in jpeg, png, webp, or gif format. Aspect ratio (width/height) must be between 0.4 and 2.5, width and height between 300 and 6000 px, and file size under 30 MB each. Cannot be combined with first_frame_url or last_frame_url.
reference_video_urlsOptional. Up to 3 videos in mp4 or mov format at 480p or 720p. Each video must be 2 to 15 seconds, with a combined total of at most 15 seconds. Aspect ratio 0.4 to 2.5, width and height 300 to 6000 px, total pixels 409,600 to 927,408, 24 to 60 FPS, and up to 50 MB each.
reference_audio_urlsOptional. Up to 3 audio clips in wav or mp3 format. Each clip must be 2 to 15 seconds, with a combined total of at most 15 seconds, and up to 15 MB each.
generate_audioOptional boolean. Default is true, which generates native synchronized audio.
resolutionOptional. 480p (which the documentation describes as "for faster generation") or 720p (described as "for balance"). Default is 720p.
aspect_ratioOptional. Accepted values: 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, 9:16, 21:9, or adaptive. Default is 16:9.
durationOptional. Video length from 4 to 15 seconds, or -1 to let the model choose the duration. Default is 5.
web_searchOptional boolean. Enables online search. Supported in text-to-video mode only.

What Seedance 2.0 Mini Generated in Our Tests

Each video was generated with Seedance 2.0 Mini on Kie.ai in October 2026. We checked that each output has an audio track but did not judge the audio itself.

Text to video: a rainy cafe window

We asked for a rainy evening outside a small cafe window with raindrops running down the glass, warm light inside, a person in a yellow raincoat walking past on the sidewalk, a slow camera push-in toward the window, and sounds of steady rain, distant traffic, and footsteps on wet pavement, at 720p, 16:9, and 5 seconds. The API returned a 1280x720 MP4 of 5.09 seconds with an audio track. The output shows rain on the glass, warm interior light, and a person in a yellow raincoat, but the camera moves through the window out into the street instead of pushing in toward the window as asked.

First frame: the robot waves

Starting from a square first-frame image of our orange robot mascot on a plain light-grey studio background, we asked for the robot to wave at the camera with its right hand, tilt its head slightly to the side, and blink its antenna lights while keeping the same design and colors, at 480p, adaptive aspect ratio, and 5 seconds. We got back a 640x640 MP4 of 5.09 seconds with an audio track. The adaptive setting kept the square shape of the input image, and the robot kept its orange color, blue eyes, and lightning-bolt chest badge and waved, but it also walked toward the camera, which the prompt did not ask for, and the head tilt is not visible.

First and last frames: studio to valley

Using the studio robot image as the first frame and an illustrated image of the robot standing on a grassy hill in a sunny valley with a river and a hot-air balloon as the last frame, we asked for a smooth camera move carrying the view from the robot in the studio out to the robot standing in the sunny valley landscape, at 480p, 16:9, and 5 seconds. The API returned an 864x496 MP4 of 5.09 seconds with an audio track. The video starts on the studio robot and ends on the valley scene of the last frame with the robot waving on the hill, but the change from studio to valley happens as a cut between about 1.5 seconds and 2.0 seconds rather than the smooth camera move requested.

Two reference images, duration -1

Passing two reference images—the studio robot image first and the valley image showing the robot in the landscape second—we asked for the robot from the first reference image to walk across the grassy valley from the second reference image toward the river, stop, and wave, with cheerful background music, at 720p, 16:9, and duration -1. The API returned a 1280x720 MP4 of 10.08 seconds with an audio track, as duration -1 let the model choose the length. In the video, the robot walks across the grassy hillside toward the river, stops at the water's edge, and waves, matching the design and colors of the reference images.

How to Use the Seedance 2.0 Mini API on Kie.ai

  • 1. Create an API Key and Authenticate

    Create a key on the API Key Management page and send it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header of every request.

  • 2. Submit a Task to createTask

    Send a POST request to /api/v1/jobs/createTask with model set to bytedance/seedance-2-mini and your chosen input mode (text-to-video, first/last frame image-to-video, or multimodal reference-to-video). You can also include a callBackUrl to receive results automatically, which is recommended in production.

  • 3. Retrieve the Generated Video

    Receive the completed task payload at your callBackUrl or poll the Get Task Details endpoint using the returned task ID to get the output MP4 URL.

Tips Before You Ship

Turn Off Audio When You Do Not Need It

generate_audio is true by default, so every video comes with an audio track unless you pass generate_audio: false. Set it to false when you only need silent clips.

Check Aspect Ratios on Reference and Last-Frame Images

The documentation specifies an aspect ratio (width/height) limit of 0.4 to 2.5 for reference_image_urls. In our October 2026 tests on Kie.ai, passing a wide banner image with an aspect ratio of 4.03 as last_frame_url also failed within about a second with the error "expected the aspect ratio to be between 0.40 and 2.50, but received image with aspect ratio: 4.03" (consuming 0 credits). Keep last-frame images within 0.4 to 2.5 as well.

Use First and Last Frame Mode for Exact Frame Matching

In multimodal reference mode, you can name a reference image as the first or last frame in your text prompt. However, according to the Kie.ai documentation, to strictly guarantee that the opening and closing frames match your provided images, use image-to-video (first and last frames) mode instead.

Account for Reference Video and Auto-Duration Billing

When your request includes reference videos, billing uses a lower per-second price multiplied by the total reference-video duration plus the output duration. When duration is set to -1, billing follows the duration actually generated.

Seedance 2.0 Mini is a ByteDance video generation model in the Seedance 2.0 series, offered on Kie.ai under the model ID bytedance/seedance-2-mini. It generates 480p or 720p videos of 4 to 15 seconds, or a model-chosen length with duration -1, from text, first/last frames, or multimodal references (up to 9 images, 3 videos, and 3 audio clips). Synchronized audio is on by default. On its Lumina site, ByteDance calls Seedance 2.0 Mini a cost-efficient option for frequent publishing and rapid concept testing.

In the documented parameters on Kie.ai, Seedance 2.0 Mini (bytedance/seedance-2-mini) outputs 480p or 720p and does not list a return_last_frame parameter, whereas Seedance 2.0 (bytedance/seedance-2) outputs 480p, 720p, or 1080p and includes return_last_frame. Both models support durations of 4 to 15 seconds or -1, up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos, and 3 reference audio clips, and web_search in text-to-video mode. See the parameter table above for details, and check the pricing cards for each model's cost. For 480p and 720p clips of up to 30 seconds, see Seedance 2.5 Flash from the Seedance 2.5 family.

In the documented parameters on Kie.ai, both Seedance 2.0 Mini (bytedance/seedance-2-mini) and Seedance 2.0 Fast (bytedance/seedance-2-fast) support 480p and 720p resolutions, durations of 4 to 15 seconds or -1, the same reference input limits (up to 9 images, 3 videos, 3 audio clips), and web_search in text-to-video mode. The documented parameter difference is that Seedance 2.0 Fast includes return_last_frame, while Seedance 2.0 Mini does not list return_last_frame in its documentation. See the parameter table above for full parameter details, and check the pricing cards for each model's cost.

Create a key on the API Key Management page and pass it in the request header when calling POST /api/v1/jobs/createTask. All models in the Kie.ai market use the same authentication method: an Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY header with the key from your Kie.ai API Key Management page.

No. Image-to-video (first frame), image-to-video (first and last frames), and multimodal reference-to-video are mutually exclusive and cannot be used in the same request; do not combine first_frame_url or last_frame_url with any reference_* field. In reference mode, a reference image can be named as the first or last frame in the prompt, but to strictly guarantee the first and last frames match the given images, use image-to-video (first and last frames). See the parameter table above for field rules.

Yes. Native synchronized audio is enabled by default via the generate_audio parameter (boolean, default true). In multimodal reference-to-video mode, you can also pass up to 3 wav or mp3 clips (2 to 15 seconds each, up to 15 seconds total, up to 15 MB each) in reference_audio_urls. See the parameter table above for specifications.

Setting duration to -1 lets the model choose the output video length instead of fixing it to a number between 4 and 15 seconds. For example, in our October 2026 test on Kie.ai with two reference images and duration set to -1, the model returned a 10.08-second MP4. When duration is -1, billing follows the duration actually generated. See the parameter table above for all duration options.
